item.text: {"facts":[{"source_id":"SRC-eb5d313be7de41a1","start_unit":2,"end_unit":2,"fact_summary":"China's Cyberspace Administration launched a two-month 2023 campaign targeting self-media accounts for rumors, false or harmful information, impersonation, and misleading content, while requiring platforms to strengthen account registration, identity verification, professional-qualification review, and content moderation.","question_ids":["4B.6","4B.9","8B.2","8B.6"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"The campaign was announced and implemented in March 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The directive was issued by the Central Cyberspace Administration under Xi Jinping's central party-state leadership.","limitations":["The document states the policy and enforcement framework but does not quantify implementation outcomes or independent review."]},{"source_id":"SRC-eb5d313be7de41a1","start_unit":3,"end_unit":4,"fact_summary":"The campaign ordered platforms to impose economic and operational penalties on violating self-media accounts, including removing followers, suspending or closing livestreaming, tipping, paid-consultation, advertising, and revenue functions, removing product links, and canceling revenue shares; it also required referral of suspected criminal activity to public security organs.","question_ids":["4B.6","4B.9","8B.2","8B.5","8B.6"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"These were specified enforcement measures for the March-May 2023 campaign.","ruler_attribution":"The measures were mandated by the Central Cyberspace Administration within Xi's party-state system.","limitations":["The source does not show how consistently penalties were applied or whether safeguards against political misuse existed."]},{"source_id":"SRC-90c7fb07a495a655","start_unit":3,"end_unit":3,"fact_summary":"Amnesty International reported that Chinese authorities' policies toward Uyghurs, Kazakhs, and other predominantly Muslim groups in Xinjiang involved crimes against humanity and other grave human-rights violations, and that COVID-19 lockdowns and compulsory quarantine at times undermined rights to health, food, and freedom of movement.","question_ids":["3B.1","3B.5","3B.7","3B.9","6B.6"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The submission was published in January 2023 for the February-March 2023 UN review and describes relevant ongoing policies.","ruler_attribution":"The findings concern Chinese authorities during Xi Jinping's rule.","limitations":["This supplied extract summarizes Amnesty's concerns without the underlying evidentiary detail or a specific 2023 incident chronology."]},{"source_id":"SRC-6c33c284c1b06037","start_unit":2,"end_unit":2,"fact_summary":"In his January 2023 Spring Festival speech, Xi stated that China had maintained economic growth, a grain harvest, stable employment and prices, poverty-elimination gains, scientific-technology achievements, ecological improvements, and social stability, while committing in 2023 to coordinate epidemic control with economic and social development, deepen reform and opening, improve economic performance, and improve people's lives.","question_ids":["5B.1","5B.6","5B.9","6B.1","6B.2","8B.1"],"polarity":"favorable","period_fit":"The speech was delivered on January 20, 2023 and set stated priorities for 2023.","ruler_attribution":"Xi made these claims and commitments as CPC general secretary, PRC president, and CMC chairman.","limitations":["The passage is an official self-report and does not independently verify the claimed results."]},{"source_id":"SRC-8568bae00097cb91","start_unit":1,"end_unit":2,"fact_summary":"After being elected to a third term as PRC president in March 2023, Xi stated that he would fulfill constitutional duties, treat national needs as his mission and people's interests as the yardstick, and implement the 20th CPC Congress strategy through high-quality development, technological self-reliance, coordinated regional development, green transition, improved social security, and basic public services.","question_ids":["5B.1","5B.6","6B.1","6B.2","6B.9","8B.1","8B.2"],"polarity":"favorable","period_fit":"The speech was delivered March 13, 2023 after his re-election.","ruler_attribution":"Xi personally stated these governing commitments in his official capacity.","limitations":["These are programmatic commitments; the supplied text does not establish execution or outcomes during 2023."]},{"source_id":"SRC-8568bae00097cb91","start_unit":2,"end_unit":2,"fact_summary":"Xi's March 2023 NPC speech called for a holistic national-security system, stronger public-security governance, modernization of the armed forces, continued implementation of one country-two systems, peaceful cross-Strait development while opposing Taiwan independence and foreign interference, and implementation of the Global Development and Global Security Initiatives.","question_ids":["1B.1","1B.2","1B.8","2B.1","2B.10","8B.1","8B.2"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"These were stated priorities in March 2023.","ruler_attribution":"Xi presented them as directives for the party and state under his leadership.","limitations":["The speech does not provide operational evidence sufficient to test the gap between rhetoric and implementation."]},{"source_id":"SRC-9d1b61a21b9a4787","start_unit":2,"end_unit":2,"fact_summary":"At the November 2023 APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting, Xi proposed innovation-driven, open, green, and inclusive regional development; support for trade and investment liberalization, WTO-centered rules, stable supply chains, digital transformation, carbon reduction, and cooperation on poverty reduction, food security, and development financing.","question_ids":["2B.1","5B.1","5B.4","5B.6","5B.9","6B.1","8B.1"],"polarity":"favorable","period_fit":"The proposals were delivered November 17, 2023.","ruler_attribution":"Xi made the proposals as China's president at the APEC leaders' meeting.","limitations":["The speech records proposals and stated policies, not independent evidence of implementation or distributional results."]},{"source_id":"SRC-9d1b61a21b9a4787","start_unit":2,"end_unit":2,"fact_summary":"Xi stated that China was implementing the Regional Comprehensive Economic Partnership to high standards, aligning rules with CPTPP and DEPA, pursuing carbon peak and neutrality, and advancing cooperation on green agriculture, sustainable cities, low-carbon energy, and marine pollution control.","question_ids":["5B.3","5B.4","5B.6","5B.9","8B.2","8B.6"],"polarity":"favorable","period_fit":"These were described as ongoing policies in November 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The commitments were presented by Xi on behalf of the Chinese government.","limitations":["The source does not independently assess compliance, enforcement, or actual environmental effects."]},{"source_id":"SRC-312a57389e2f85ae","start_unit":2,"end_unit":2,"fact_summary":"At the November 2023 APEC CEO Summit, Xi cited regional outcomes including a reduction in average Asia-Pacific tariffs from 17 percent to 5 percent over three decades, a contribution of 70 percent of global economic growth, more than a fourfold increase in per-capita income, and one billion people lifted from poverty.","question_ids":["5B.7","5B.10","6B.10","8B.7"],"polarity":"favorable","period_fit":"The quantitative claims were made November 16, 2023 and cover the preceding three decades rather than only 2023.","ruler_attribution":"Xi presented these regional results in his official speech.","limitations":["The figures concern the Asia-Pacific collectively and are not attributable solely to Xi or China."]},{"source_id":"SRC-312a57389e2f85ae","start_unit":2,"end_unit":2,"fact_summary":"Xi stated that China had removed all restrictive measures on foreign investment in manufacturing, was expanding market access, applying high standards to RCEP, aligning with CPTPP and DEPA rules, and seeking a market-oriented, law-based business environment with stronger foreign-investor and intellectual-property protections.","question_ids":["5B.3","5B.4","5B.6","8B.2","8B.6"],"polarity":"favorable","period_fit":"These policies and commitments were described in November 2023.","ruler_attribution":"Xi announced or reaffirmed them as China's president.","limitations":["The passage does not provide independent verification of the legal changes or enforcement quality."]},{"source_id":"SRC-312a57389e2f85ae","start_unit":2,"end_unit":2,"fact_summary":"Xi reported that the third Belt and Road Forum produced 458 deliverables, Chinese financial institutions established an RMB 780 billion financing window for Belt and Road projects, and Chinese and foreign companies reached USD 97.2 billion in business deals.","question_ids":["5B.6","5B.10","8B.3","8B.6"],"polarity":"favorable","period_fit":"The forum and figures were reported in November 2023, referring to the forum held in October 2023.","ruler_attribution":"Xi reported these outcomes for an initiative he proposed and led politically.","limitations":["The supplied source does not detail disbursement, project completion, debt effects, or independent auditing."]},{"source_id":"SRC-2b6b8de5330b3015","start_unit":2,"end_unit":2,"fact_summary":"At a November 2023 welcome dinner in the United States, Xi stated that he and President Biden had agreed to increase direct passenger flights, hold a high-level tourism dialogue, streamline visa procedures, and cooperate on diplomacy, trade, people-to-people exchange, education, science, agriculture, military, law enforcement, and artificial intelligence.","question_ids":["1B.8","2B.1","2B.7","8B.9"],"polarity":"favorable","period_fit":"The commitments followed the Xi-Biden meeting in November 2023.","ruler_attribution":"Xi publicly described bilateral agreements reached with President Biden.","limitations":["The supplied text does not document subsequent implementation or durability."]},{"source_id":"SRC-2b6b8de5330b3015","start_unit":2,"end_unit":2,"fact_summary":"Xi stated that China and the United States agreed to establish a counternarcotics working group, and he announced that China would invite 50,000 young Americans to China for exchange and study programs over the following five years.","question_ids":["2B.1","2B.7","8B.2","8B.9"],"polarity":"favorable","period_fit":"The commitments were announced November 15, 2023.","ruler_attribution":"Xi announced the measures in the context of his meeting with President Biden.","limitations":["The source does not show whether the working group or exchange program became operational."]},{"source_id":"SRC-2b6b8de5330b3015","start_unit":3,"end_unit":3,"fact_summary":"Xi claimed that China had lifted 100 million people out of the UN poverty-line category through eight years of effort and had achieved the UN 2030 Agenda poverty-reduction goal ten years ahead of schedule.","question_ids":["5B.1","5B.8","5B.10","6B.1","6B.10","8B.7"],"polarity":"favorable","period_fit":"The claim was made in November 2023 and concerns results achieved before and during Xi's tenure.","ruler_attribution":"Xi attributed the result to CPC-led efforts under his leadership.","limitations":["The supplied source provides no independent methodology, distributional breakdown, or attribution analysis."]},{"source_id":"SRC-2b6b8de5330b3015","start_unit":3,"end_unit":3,"fact_summary":"Xi stated that China had close to half of the world's installed photovoltaic capacity, more than half of the world's new-energy vehicles on its roads, and one-fourth of the world's increase in afforestation area, while pledging carbon dioxide peaking before 2030 and carbon neutrality before 2060.","question_ids":["5B.6","5B.10","8B.6","8B.7"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"The figures and pledges were presented in November 2023, with targets extending beyond the period.","ruler_attribution":"Xi presented the achievements and climate commitments as China's leader.","limitations":["The claims are official statements and do not establish whether emissions targets are sufficient or implementation is durable."]},{"source_id":"SRC-55e4268835e1e5f3","start_unit":4,"end_unit":5,"fact_summary":"Human Rights Watch reported that after the abrupt end of zero-Covid restrictions in late 2022, infections, hospitalizations, and deaths surged; official authorities estimated 60,000 excess deaths in December 2022, while a US academic study estimated 1.87 million deaths between December 2022 and January 2023, with the true toll obscured by censorship.","question_ids":["3B.9","6B.6","6B.5","7B.1","7B.2"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The reported mortality period overlaps January 2023, while the policy reversal occurred in late 2022.","ruler_attribution":"The report concerns the Chinese government under Xi Jinping.","limitations":["The estimates differ substantially and the supplied extract does not resolve the true mortality figure."]},{"source_id":"SRC-55e4268835e1e5f3","start_unit":4,"end_unit":5,"fact_summary":"Human Rights Watch reported continuing repression of Uyghurs and other Turkic Muslims in Xinjiang, restrictions on contacts abroad and cultural, linguistic, and religious advocacy in Xinjiang and Tibet, expanded social controls, and the absence of independent civil society.","question_ids":["3B.1","3B.2","3B.5","3B.7","3B.8","4B.3","4B.7"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The report covers events and conditions during 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The findings concern Chinese government policy under Xi Jinping.","limitations":["This is an external human-rights assessment; the extract does not provide the full underlying case documentation."]},{"source_id":"SRC-55e4268835e1e5f3","start_unit":4,"end_unit":5,"fact_summary":"In 2023, authorities released Wuhan reporter Fang Bin after three years in detention, but activist and former lawyer Zhang Zhan remained imprisoned and was transferred to a prison hospital in July because of deteriorating health; a court sentenced Uyghur student Kamile Wayit to three years for sharing a video of the 2022 protests.","question_ids":["3B.1","3B.4","3B.8","4B.3","4B.6"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The releases, continued detention, transfer, and sentence occurred in 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The actions were taken by Chinese authorities and courts under Xi's government.","limitations":["The source does not establish Xi's personal involvement in each case."]},{"source_id":"SRC-55e4268835e1e5f3","start_unit":5,"end_unit":6,"fact_summary":"Authorities fined a comedy company RMB 14.7 million for a comedian's joke about the PLA, suspended a Malaysian comedian's Weibo account, sentenced economist Yang Shaozheng to 4.5 years for inciting subversion after criticizing government personnel costs, and relied on technology companies to enforce extensive censorship.","question_ids":["3B.3","3B.8","4B.3","4B.6","4B.9"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The penalties and censorship findings were reported for 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The measures were imposed by Chinese authorities and state-linked platforms under Xi's leadership.","limitations":["The source does not establish whether Xi personally ordered these individual cases."]},{"source_id":"SRC-55e4268835e1e5f3","start_unit":6,"end_unit":6,"fact_summary":"China's September 2023 religious-venue measures required religious sites to indoctrinate followers in CPC ideology, restricted unapproved funding, and followed continued arrests, detention, harassment, and alteration or demolition of Muslim religious sites; authorities also transferred a Catholic bishop to Shanghai without consulting the Vatican, contrary to the 2018 accord.","question_ids":["3B.1","3B.5","3B.7","4B.3","4B.4","7B.7"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The measures and transfer occurred in 2023, while the broader policy dates from Xi's 2016 call for religious Sinicization.","ruler_attribution":"The policies were implemented by Chinese authorities under Xi's party-state leadership.","limitations":["The extract reports HRW's assessment and does not provide the government's full legal justification."]},{"source_id":"SRC-55e4268835e1e5f3","start_unit":6,"end_unit":7,"fact_summary":"In 2023, Chinese authorities sentenced legal scholar Xu Zhiyong and lawyer Ding Jiaxi to 14 and 12 years, respectively; arrested lawyer Yu Wensheng and his wife; detained or placed other lawyers under house arrest; and sentenced activist Guo Feixiong to eight years for inciting subversion.","question_ids":["3B.1","3B.4","3B.8","4B.3","4B.4"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The arrests, detentions, and sentences were reported as 2023 events, although some underlying prosecutions began earlier.","ruler_attribution":"The actions were taken by Chinese courts and security authorities under Xi's government.","limitations":["The source does not establish direct personal instructions from Xi."]},{"source_id":"SRC-55e4268835e1e5f3","start_unit":7,"end_unit":8,"fact_summary":"Human Rights Watch reported that Hong Kong authorities had arrested at least 279 people under the National Security Law or sedition law, with national-security prosecutions having a 100 percent conviction rate at the time of reporting; authorities also restricted protests, targeted publications, and issued warrants and bounties against eight overseas activists.","question_ids":["3B.1","3B.5","3B.8","4B.2","4B.3","4B.4","4B.9"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The report describes the situation during 2023 and cumulative enforcement since the 2020 National Security Law.","ruler_attribution":"The Hong Kong measures operated under Beijing's policy framework during Xi's leadership.","limitations":["The source does not distinguish all Hong Kong decisions from direct central-government orders."]},{"source_id":"SRC-55e4268835e1e5f3","start_unit":8,"end_unit":9,"fact_summary":"In 2023, a Hong Kong court ruled unconstitutional the requirement that transgender men undergo full sex-reassignment surgery to change legal gender, and the top court ordered the government to establish a framework recognizing same-sex partnerships.","question_ids":["3B.4","3B.7","4B.4","4B.7"],"polarity":"favorable","period_fit":"The rulings occurred in February and September 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The findings concern Hong Kong courts and government institutions operating under the broader sovereignty framework of Xi's government.","limitations":["These were judicial decisions in Hong Kong and are not evidence of a comparable mainland policy change."]},{"source_id":"SRC-55e4268835e1e5f3","start_unit":8,"end_unit":8,"fact_summary":"Human Rights Watch reported that an estimated half-million Uyghurs and other Turkic Muslims remained imprisoned in 2023, with no mass releases; Xi visited Xinjiang in August and described his policies there as a success despite a UN report detailing possible crimes against humanity.","question_ids":["3B.1","3B.2","3B.5","3B.7","7B.2","7B.10"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The prison estimate and Xi's visit occurred in 2023, while the detentions began during the 2017 crackdown.","ruler_attribution":"Xi publicly endorsed the Xinjiang policy during his August 2023 visit.","limitations":["The detention estimate is attributed to Human Rights Watch and the supplied extract does not provide a complete denominator or case list."]},{"source_id":"SRC-55e4268835e1e5f3","start_unit":9,"end_unit":10,"fact_summary":"Revisions to China's Women’s Rights and Interests Protection Law took effect on January 1, 2023 and addressed workplace discrimination and sexual harassment, but Human Rights Watch reported persistent difficulties obtaining accountability and questioned the amendments' effectiveness; China also experienced more deaths than births for the first time in six decades.","question_ids":["3B.7","4B.7","5B.8","6B.2","6B.8","8B.6","8B.7"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"The legal revisions and demographic result were reported for 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The law was enacted and administered by the Chinese party-state under Xi's leadership.","limitations":["The demographic change reflects longer-term trends and cannot be attributed solely to 2023 policy."]},{"source_id":"SRC-55e4268835e1e5f3","start_unit":10,"end_unit":10,"fact_summary":"In 2023, the Beijing LGBT Center closed, multiple LGBT organizations and public accounts were banned on WeChat, and LGBT activists faced increased harassment and censorship.","question_ids":["3B.7","3B.8","4B.3","4B.7","4B.9"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The closures and account bans occurred in May and August 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The actions involved Chinese authorities and major platforms operating under Xi-era censorship controls.","limitations":["The source does not establish whether each closure was directly ordered by central authorities."]},{"source_id":"SRC-55e4268835e1e5f3","start_unit":10,"end_unit":11,"fact_summary":"China remained the world's largest greenhouse-gas emitter and coal producer and consumer; Human Rights Watch reported that its domestic emissions target was rated highly insufficient for the Paris Agreement's 1.5-degree goal, despite China leading global renewable-energy production.","question_ids":["5B.6","5B.9","5B.10","6B.6","8B.7"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"The assessment concerns China's position and policies during 2023, with climate targets extending beyond the period.","ruler_attribution":"The national energy and climate trajectory occurred under Xi's government.","limitations":["The assessment combines national-level outcomes with a rating by Climate Action Tracker and does not isolate Xi's personal decisions."]},{"source_id":"SRC-55e4268835e1e5f3","start_unit":11,"end_unit":11,"fact_summary":"In 2023, Chinese authorities raided the Beijing office of Mintz Group, raided Bain's Shanghai office, required staff of Franklin Templeton and BlackRock to attend classes on Xi Jinping Thought, and made vague amendments to the Counter-Espionage Law that increased uncertainty for foreign businesses.","question_ids":["4B.2","4B.5","4B.6","5B.4","5B.7","7B.7"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The raids, classes, and legal amendments occurred in 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The measures were taken by Chinese state authorities under Xi's leadership and explicitly promoted Xi Jinping Thought.","limitations":["The source does not quantify economic effects or establish Xi's personal involvement in each enforcement action."]},{"source_id":"SRC-55e4268835e1e5f3","start_unit":11,"end_unit":12,"fact_summary":"Human Rights Watch reported that Xi continued crucial support for Russia despite sanctions over its full-scale invasion of Ukraine, met Vladimir Putin shortly after the International Criminal Court issued an arrest warrant for Putin, and hosted Syria's Bashar al-Assad, who is alleged to have committed war crimes.","question_ids":["2B.1","2B.2","2B.5","2B.9","2B.10","7B.7"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The meetings and support described occurred in 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The foreign-policy decisions and meetings were undertaken by Xi or his government.","limitations":["The extract does not detail the precise material scope of support to Russia or the legal positions underlying the meetings."]},{"source_id":"SRC-55e4268835e1e5f3","start_unit":12,"end_unit":12,"fact_summary":"Chinese diplomats were reported to have harassed civil-society representatives at the UN Human Rights Council and sent notes discouraging governments from attending civil-society events concerning Xinjiang and press freedom in Hong Kong.","question_ids":["2B.6","3B.4","4B.3","4B.6","7B.6","7B.7"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The described diplomatic actions occurred in 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The actions were carried out by Chinese diplomats representing Xi's government.","limitations":["The source does not identify the individual officials responsible or record any formal response by Xi."]}],"documents_with_no_material_fact":["SRC-9bd957db8c2d9484","SRC-e4bc086640ef71fa","SRC-d491faf252523e33"],"batch_limitations":["The supplied extracts are predominantly official speeches, webpage summaries, or external assessments; many programmatic claims lack independent 2023 implementation or outcome verification.","Several sources describe cumulative policies or conditions spanning multiple years. Facts were included only when the supplied units provided a concrete event, policy, quantitative result, or institutional finding relevant to 2023-2023."]}
